analysis: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis is a rare but serious complication that occurs due to a paradoxical hypercoagulable state. This is primarily associated with Protein C deficiency. Warfarin inhibits vitamin K-dependent clotting factors, including Protein C, which is a natural anticoagulant. In individuals with Protein C deficiency, the rapid decrease in Protein C levels upon initiation of warfarin therapy can lead to a temporary hypercoagulable state, resulting in skin necrosis. While Protein S deficiency could theoretically contribute to a similar state, it is less commonly implicated in this specific condition. Hemophilia and Antithrombin III deficiency are not typically associated with warfarin-induced skin necrosis, as they do not involve the same mechanisms affected by warfarin. Therefore, based on standard medical knowledge and consensus, Protein C deficiency is the most likely cause of warfarin-induced skin necrosis.
